assessment_scope.source_boundary: Only the subject's two curated REVIEWED items at basis_commit, each read in full with its front matter: the canonical KSOA-G1 character monograph series/kamakura-sho/studies/KSOA_MOTOYA_KITSUKAWA.md and the canonical directed partnership study series/kamakura-sho/studies/KSOA_PARTNERSHIP.md. Both are repository literary analysis of the seven Japanese publisher novels (文春文庫) through V07 EPI p[0151] and KSOA-V07-H-0015. The ledgers, deep readings, claim-revision entries and the project's reconstruction specification and readiness audit that these studies link are not curated on this subject; the ledger and reading locators cited below are quoted from the two studies as their own citations, and no claim rests on unread linked material. No primary-source inspection was performed.
assessment_scope.temporal_boundary: Motoya Kitsukawa from V01 (rank pride, independent questions about Ashina's health and the Torii article connection) through V02 workplace verification, apology support and accepted off-duty request, V03 economic reading, evidence presentation and identified-officer stay, V04 complementary footage proposal and requested questioning lead, V05 off-duty craft interview, self-recognized attraction and arrest, V06 Mizutani omission, Kosugi and taxi alibi limits, deferral recommendation, Emiri omission and family narrative, to V07 authorized-release boundary, concealed private meeting, photograph recognition, smaller self-judgment and the private pledge at EPI p[0135]-p[0151] as endpoint. Capability states split at located changes: before V05 his attraction to Emiri is absent; within V07 his reading of Emiri's affection holds until the epilogue discloses her private relation to Izumida (EPI p[0087]-p[0143]), and his resolve to support Asumi is formed only at the finale and is not known to Asumi. Whether he discloses or acts on the pledge is outside the seven novels.
assessment_scope.assessment_method: characters/RECONSTRUCTION_CAPABILITY_SPEC.md and governance/policies/CHARACTER_RECONSTRUCTION_MAINTENANCE.md at basis_commit, applying the owner calibration rulings recorded there (B/C boundary, single counting of uncertainty, dialogue constrained-use test, chronology splits, relationship-transfer safeguards and control-state attribution); evidence-located calibration with countercases, explicit gaps and no model-readiness inheritance.

dimensions.note: The monograph gives an explicit interpretation: he notices when a proposed explanation outruns the evidence while making similarly hopeful leaps about people he likes; his firmer work takes concrete forms (locating a record, a follow-up question, marking what can be said publicly); and a gap separates visible competence from self-appraisal. It predicts a characteristic error: accommodating acceptance of a liked person's account (V06 Emiri distance from Nonaka; V06 Yakushiji's candor; V07 projection corrected by the epilogue), while his evidence standard holds (V07 authorized release, refusing a fan's assurance, asking for a corroborator). Not B: the studies list contributing factors for off-duty help (childhood obligation, being identified, local civilians, Asumi's appeals, resentment) without saying which decides, and present the V06 deferral and omission as acts with different bases without resolving the motive; that is insufficiency, not productive uncertainty. The witness-evaluation domain is B-like, but this whole-subject record does not establish a discriminating account elsewhere. Not D: an explicit, located account with a predicted error type supports narrow extrapolation.

The partnership table gives a directed state for each volume V01-V07, and the monograph traces a development from bruised rank pride (V01) to defined contributions (V02-V06) to a smaller self-judgment despite praise and a changed description of his future role (V07). Not B: apart from the V07 finale, the changes are not causally sequenced or located as state transitions. Not D: per-volume states and the endpoint are explicit.

The monograph states that his speech tracks audience: formal identification at the first scene, rank used as a mock honorific with Asumi, 俺 and surname address in ordinary talk with her, 吉川です in V07 official introduction, 僕 with Nagasaka, and courteous and more familiar turns in the private meeting; it distinguishes narrated hesitation from the calm phrasing others hear. Not B: few utterances are quoted and no sentence-level rule is given. Not D: address and self-reference are analyzed across audiences and functions.

The monograph records preferences beyond case work: familiar food when tired (V06 C01 p[0870]-p[0899]), a newly acquired taste and attention to Izumida's competence at the V07 counter, and a family narrative explaining why salaried work feels more secure (V06 C02 p[0509]-p[0515]). Not C: these are located in two volumes without a conditional account of ordinary choices. Not E: they are distributed and tied to explained background.

The partnership table gives directed, located states toward Asumi for every volume, and the studies separately analyze Emiri (attraction affecting evaluation, V05; omitted connection, V06; misread affection, V07), Sayaka (interview modeling ordinary questions, V05; qualified fact under challenge, V06), Yakushiji and Nagasaka. Address changes are read as changes of function, not steady escalation. Not B: the studies do not say which conditions decide whether he helps Asumi off duty or how far he resists her lead. Not D: the deltas are directed and located.

As primary focalizer, his inner states are narrated in every volume and the studies analyze their relation to speech and action: injured pride that hears an invitation as condescension (V01), resentment that does not undo help (V02, V05), private concern about witness pressure (V03), inward qualification of Asumi's account and withdrawal from the quarrel (V06), mock deference that protests inwardly, recognition that attraction may bias him (V05), a smaller self-judgment despite praise and the unheard pledge (V07). Not A: two short studies, no catalogue of inner voice and no test of predictions. Not C: interior access is direct and repeated rather than inferred from action.

Interpersonal conflict is located and interpreted: declining Asumi's emotional overture (V02), withdrawing from the V06 bar quarrel, reporting sensitive information despite anticipated friction (V06), keeping the V07 meeting from Asumi because he anticipates conflict, and challenging the line from grievance to action (V07). Not B: the studies do not explain why he reports in V06 but conceals in V07 beyond noting the acts have different consequences, and physical confrontation (the V05 arrest) is not analyzed. Not D: an avoidance tendency and its countercase are located.

Because he is focalized, part of his weighing is represented: private questioning of pressure on witnesses (V03), keeping his name out of the piece (V05), a qualified fact under Sayaka's challenge and Yakushiji's possible responsibility treated as a distinct post-event matter (V06), and the V07 limit to the authorized release with a corroborator required. Not B: his private decision whether to report the V07 meeting and the V06 omission are not explained by a stated rule. Not D: located judgments with reasons are analyzed.

Humor appears only locally: rank used as a mock honorific with Asumi and his inward protest under it. No humorous conduct is analyzed beyond that. Not D: there is no distributed body of humorous conduct.

Both items cover V01-V07, a complete series, with located contributions in every volume and the endpoint V07 EPI p[0151]. Not B: two short studies (about 20 KB) are the whole curated set, with no operational model, ledger entries or probe curated on this subject. Not D: every volume has located analysis.

Affirmative located limits: his V07 projection about Emiri fails when the epilogue discloses her reason (cited to V07 CL-0005-R01); his favorable reading of Yakushiji is vulnerable to Asumi's performance hypothesis (V06); the pledge is internal and Asumi cannot hear it; it follows earlier support and is not the first instance of care; outsider labels and his action have distinct sources (V02); the romantic reading has limited authority. Not B: few limits and none tested. Not D: each is located.

Claims carry volume anchors, several page anchors (V06 C01-C02, V07 C01, C03-C04 and EPI), an explicit endpoint at V07 EPI p[0151], the epilogue split of his knowledge about Emiri, and the rule that the pledge's disclosure lies outside the novels. Not B: no knowledge views are given for earlier states. Not D: the endpoint and the within-volume split are explicit.

conditions: Use is illustrative reconstruction of a named V01-V07 state, never attributed quotation; Japanese lines presented as canon are retrieved from the witnesses.

Self-reference and address follow the sampled audiences: 俺 and surname with Asumi, mock rank title in deference-protest, 吉川です in official introduction, 僕 with Nagasaka; unsampled audiences are lower confidence.
Narrated hesitation is inner response; spoken lines heard by others are calmer, and an inner pledge or judgment is not voiced unless the scenario states it.

Not READY: few utterances are quoted and no sentence-level rule is given. Not NOT_READY: the sampled audiences and functions are analyzed.

conditions: Change one fact of a case, witness relationship or assignment at a time from a named state, and state it.
Predict an evidence-bounded answer on authorized information but a more accommodating reading of a witness he likes; mark off-duty help and disclosure to Asumi as low confidence.

cross_scenario_scope.interlocutor_relationship: Asumi as his senior partner and childhood acquaintance, a civilian witness or expert, a superior, or Sayaka as an off-duty acquaintance and journalist.

No cross-series settings or changed institutional roles without a stated assumption.

scenario_readiness.note: His concrete contributions, evidence standard and accommodating error are located and repeated, which supports bounded counterfactuals inside comparable investigative work. Not READY: what decides off-duty help and concealment is unresolved. Not NOT_READY: the contribution and error patterns recur across volumes.

conditions: Limited to off-duty or work-adjacent scenes with Asumi, Sayaka or known local figures (meals, counters, invited help), using the located preferences and resentment-with-help pattern.
Family, romantic and unfamiliar social settings beyond the V06 family narrative require abstention.
scenario_readiness.note: Off-duty scenes, food preferences and family background support narrow situated interpretation. Not READY: ordinary choices have no conditional account. Not NOT_READY: several off-duty and counter scenes are analyzed.

conditions: Decisions about what case information to release, how to question a witness and whether an account needs corroboration, at a named state.
Whether he reports a private contact to Asumi or omits a liked witness's connection is not predicted beyond the sampled V06 and V07 cases.
scenario_readiness.note: His information-release and witness-handling judgments are represented with reasons. Not READY: his private reporting decisions are not explained by a rule. Not NOT_READY: located reasoning exists, unlike for his partner.

The partnership study gives the romantic reading limited authority and leaves the development of their reliance outside work open, his V07 reading of Emiri's affection is a corrected misreading, and the pledge's disclosure lies outside the novels. Not CONDITIONAL: the evidence affirmatively withholds a romantic trajectory rather than being silent.

conditions: Record checks, concrete follow-up questions, footage or alibi verification, evidence presentation and public-statement limits as a 巡査長 working with Asumi, at a named state.
Initiative is not fixed: he can propose and lead (V04) or follow a strong lead while challenging its links (V07); state the assignment and rank context.
scenario_readiness.note: Located investigative contributions in every volume support bounded professional reconstruction. Not READY: his initiative relative to Asumi and his reporting choices vary without a stated rule. Not NOT_READY: the contribution forms recur.

known_limits.statement: He accepts liked people's accounts too readily: Emiri's distance from Nonaka (V06), Yakushiji's candor (V06) and his V07 projection, which the epilogue corrects.

Personal hope does not move his evidence standard on authorized information: in V07 he limits his answer to the authorized release, does not let a fan's assurance exclude a witness and asks for a corroborator.
The V07 resolve to support Asumi is internal; Asumi cannot hear it, it is not the first instance of his care, and whether he discloses or acts on it is outside the seven novels.
A romantic reading of the partnership has limited authority; the best-supported ending is professional and interpersonal reliance with its development outside work left open.
The studies do not say which conditions decide his off-duty help or his choice between reporting (V06) and concealing (V07) private contacts.
The curated set is two short literary studies; no operational model, validation probe or ledger entries are curated on this subject.

assessment_scope.source_boundary: Only the subject's two curated REVIEWED items at basis_commit, each read in full with its front matter: the canonical v2.0 self-contained character monograph KSOA_MOTOYA_KITSUKAWA.md (general revision of 2026-11-15 reconciled with the independent KSOA-CB1 baseline; every Japanese quotation checked against its witness line; acceptance review self-containment PASS and fidelity PASS after fourteen recorded fixes) and the canonical v1.1 relationship study KSOA_PARTNERSHIP.md. Both analyse the seven accepted Japanese publisher EPUB witnesses (V01-V07, through V07 EPI p[0151] and KSOA-V07-H-0015) and both mark themselves do_not_use_as_literary_evidence: they are analysis, not quotation sources. Motoya is the close-third focalizer outside the reader-only prologues and the opening concert scene of V02 C01 [p0014-p0170], which is focalized through station chief Takanashi Hideo. The monograph keeps his narrated interiority (INT), his speech and acts (OBS), narratorial exposition (NARR), testimony (TEST), its own inference (INF) and speculation (SPEC) apart; this record does the same. The ledgers, deep readings, CB1 adjudication records, qualification record and project reconstruction specification they link were read only as method context; none is curated on this subject and no claim rests on them. Asumi Ogasawara's monograph and capability state are not borrowed. The monograph's section 15 profile is, by its own statement, untested and ungraded. No primary source was inspected.
assessment_scope.temporal_boundary: Motoya across the complete seven-novel series, V01 (late spring 2022, about thirty, a 巡査長 in 強行六係) through the V07 epilogue (31 July-5 August, year unprinted, about thirty-one), bound by volume. Located distributions, not absolute period rules: おまえ to Asumi is frequent in V01 (about fourteen), continues in V02-V03 (four and three), is absent in V04, occurs once in V05 in genuine anger [C02 p0789] and is absent in V06-V07; 僕 in his own dialogue begins in V05 (one V03 parody excepted) and is never addressed to Asumi; Sayaka Takigawa and Emiri Hatano belong to V05-V07. Located within-volume changes: V04 from 'cannot state a wish to a 管理官' [C01 p0885] to proposing and leading Miyazaki's questioning [C03 p0473-p0598]; the V05 café anger [C02 p0785-p0789]; the V06 dawn correction and report [C03 p0240-p0264]; the V07 epilogue blackout, overheard acknowledgement, private pledge and second blackout [EPI p0131-p0149]. Family, schools, past girlfriends and the old wound are prior conditions disclosed late, not development, and belong to him at every earlier state. The boundary limits evidence, not his knowledge; he has no access to Asumi's interior and never learns more of his own past within the series.
assessment_scope.assessment_method: characters/RECONSTRUCTION_CAPABILITY_SPEC.md and governance/policies/CHARACTER_RECONSTRUCTION_MAINTENANCE.md at basis_commit, including the owner calibration rulings; evidence-located calibration with countercases, explicit gaps and no model-readiness inheritance.

dimensions.note: The monograph's section 15 states sixteen conditional rules (R1-R16), each with trigger, perception, response, counterconditions, counterexamples, support level and abstention, built on narrated interiority across seven volumes: doubt-then-yield to Asumi's unbased lines of inquiry, public backing with private objection, silence or a short jab at teasing against anger at an attack on his integrity, obedience to superiors with initiative once facts are in hand, release discipline, liking that lowers his demand for verification, and the hope-then-shame pattern toward gentle women. It predicts his mistakes (settling early on the obvious about a person's inner life, misreading motive rooted in love or shame, trusting a likeable performer) as well as his sound calls (concealment detection, structural priors). Not A: the profile is untested by its own statement, and his motive-reading accuracy is explicitly mixed and qualitative. Not C: within investigative, partnership and civilian-friend conduct the account says what changes his response (facts in hand, audience, order from a 管理官, integrity versus pride, liking or hope, accountability).

Section 14 gives volume-by-volume development, revelation and stable features, a five-item list of supported changes (scope and consequence of his credit to Asumi; おまえ fading; separation of attraction from judgement; initiative with superiors; response to integrity attacks) and an explicit list of what only appears to change; the partnership study adds directed states per volume. Not B: the causes of the おまえ change and of 僕 are recorded as unresolved, the attraction-separation trend rests on three points with the first inferred, and the integrity-response change on two. Not D: each volume carries separately evidenced states with locators and a stated distinction between development and late disclosure.

Section 9 analyses written Japanese by recipient and period: self-reference (俺 with Asumi and colleagues; わたし, わたしたち and 我々 for duty; 僕 with civilians from V05 only, with the V03 parody exception), address in both directions with counts (おまえ by volume; Asumi's キミ by volume; 小笠原, デカチョウ, こいつ), register shifts (rough casual with Asumi, officialese when she fumbles, textbook law for the anxious, stammer under pressure, politeness repair before women he wants to please, plain bluntness with exposed suspects, deadpan understatement), characteristic expressions and three thought-against-speech rules with narration-certified sincerity markers. Not A: whether 僕 is development or exposure is unresolved, most forms are exemplified rather than counted, and tone is only narrated. Not C: forms are tied to recipient, function, pressure and period with stated exceptions.

Section 11 classifies ordinary conduct by number of independent occasions: coffee across all seven volumes judged with some precision; cheap filling meals by default (V01, V03, V06, V07); restaurant choice left to Asumi; sensory appreciation of good food when served; aversion to luxury prices; drinking at six of seven case-end celebrations; films on a subscription service, sea air and walking; heat and damp futons as aversions; hometown attachment; on-duty and off-duty clothing; R13 gives a conditional food rule. Not A: home routine beyond the coffee server and a bar near home, hobbies, cooking and family life are recorded as not established. Not C: repeated patterns are separated from single choices and conditioned (tired, served, priced, deferring).

Directed conduct per relationship: toward Asumi a private ledger with positive and negative columns, public backing, private objection, grudging caretaking, concealment of private meetings, siding with her against Sayaka and full credit in V07, with the partnership study's directed state table; Sayaka and Emiri as separate courses (V05-V07); superiors by name (Masaki, Nikaidō, Satake, Yoshida) with obedience and managing up; colleagues; classes of witnesses and suspects (men of status, elderly men, earnest craftspeople, women in the cases, suspects in custody). Not A: his family appears in no scene, and Asumi's side is reachable only through his readings. Not C: what changes his conduct with each partner (witnesses present, superior's order, liking, friction with Asumi) is stated, with counterexamples.

As focalizer his beliefs, appraisals and self-reproach are narrated throughout; section 7 separates private interpretation, utterance, professional action and misjudgement in tables with locators, and records that his thought is both harsher and kinder about Asumi than his speech, that his hesitation is mostly interior, and that narration marks the rare moments when speech and thought coincide (本音). Not A: interior links the monograph itself marks as inference stay open (whether attraction steered the V03 camera thought; why he never asks what Asumi's suspicion implies; the content of the old wound), so novel interior monologue would extend beyond what is evidenced. Not C: the interior is directly attested and systematically mapped against speech and action.

Response families are located and conditioned: short jabs or silence at teasing (anger would only entertain her), revenge teasing about handsome men, genuine anger and おまえ when his integrity is attacked (V05) and reasoned irritation at the same insinuation a month later (V06), panic and fluster before Sayaka, escape from the V06 bar quarrel, concealment to avoid friction with a brief truthful answer and silence when caught (V07), private objection to Asumi's ethics where it touches his private life (V05), and feigned compliance with superiors. Not A: open confrontation with a superior, physical danger and Asumi doing harm are never tested. Not C: triggers, inhibitors and counterexamples are specified for each conflict type.

Unlike a non-focal character, his weighing is narrated: the V02 secrecy promise reasoned from likely reprimand rather than principle [C03 p0463-p0469]; the V06 vouching and omission with separate bases (an overstated assurance, and convenience) [C01 p0591-p0607] followed by an honest report of Emiri's correction despite anticipated friction [C03 p0240, p0264]; the V07 role-over-wish answer with his disturbed heart narrated [C04 p0187-p0189]; refusal of reward citing public-servant status; release discipline from V01; and conventional moral reflection voiced almost entirely inwardly. Not A: high-stakes conflicts (concealing a suspect, Asumi wrong in a way that harms someone) are untested, and reflection rarely changes his action. Not C: the bases of his choices are narrated and distinguished, including self-interested ones.

His humour is described as mostly deadpan or retaliatory: 'you will live long', mock-formal デカチョウどの praise sincere in content, mock praise that backfires when Asumi accepts it, deadpan understatement at a stake-out and to a patrol officer, revenge teasing about handsome men. Not B: few occasions and no account of when he initiates play rather than retaliating. Not D: the functions (retaliation, understatement, praise in a teasing register) and their audiences are analysed.

The complete admitted series is covered; the monograph's revision record reports the project's qualification record listing it COMPLETE_AT_BOUNDARY, it gives 40 traced load-bearing claims with native locators, and was reconciled with an independent blind baseline whose acceptance review's defects are recorded as fixed; his evidence is the densest in the series because narration runs through him. Not A: no scene with his family, almost no stated career ambition, the unexplained old wound, no physical description and no interview conducted alone under a superior's observation. Not C: the analysis covers the whole admitted corpus and distinguishes these gaps from documented facts.

Affirmative limits with locators: because his interior is visible throughout, the absence of narrated romantic desire for Asumi and of jealousy is affirmative counterevidence on his side, with one disowned bodily moment [V01 EPI p0067]; he never contradicts Asumi in front of others; he never presses an evasive witness hard without facts in hand; no leak of case information is shown; he refuses reward; every narrated romantic hope fails; and his V07 projection about Emiri is corrected by the epilogue. Not A: several limits are 'never shown' rather than tested. Not C: the limits are evidenced, including the affirmative romance case.

Narrated time is dated (May 2022 to early August 2023), development is separated from late revelation in a table with first disclosure points, address is distributed per volume, and within-volume changes are located for V04, V05, V06 and the V07 epilogue; the profile tells the user to bind any rendering to a period (おまえ only before V04 or in anger, 僕 from V05). Not A: the causes of the changes are mostly unstated and the V07 year is unprinted. Not C: the period conditions are explicit and evidenced.

conditions: Illustrative written-Japanese lines only, never presented as quotation; choose the action family first, then the register.

Bind wording to the located volume and recipient: 俺, 小笠原 and plain speech with Asumi, with おまえ only in V01-V03 or as a single angry use (V05); わたし and です/ます with witnesses and superiors; 僕 and a soft polite register with civilians from V05 on, never to Asumi; blunt plain speech with exposed suspects. These are observed distributions, not categorical rules.
Keep his thought harsher, and sometimes kinder, than his speech and let him swallow the sharpest line; voice anger only at an attack on his integrity, fluster before an attractive woman, or drunk.
No acoustic voice, no family dialogue and no sober explicit conversation about the relationship with Asumi.
scenario_readiness.note: Section 9's self-reference table, two-way address counts and register shifts, with section 15's 'choose speech after behaviour' rule, constrain short written-Japanese lines in the sampled relationships. Not READY: tone is only narrated, the 僕 question is open and most forms are exemplified rather than counted. Not NOT_READY: forms are tied to recipient, period and pressure with exceptions.

conditions: Predict action families from R1-R16: doubt-then-yield to Asumi's unbased lines, public backing and private objection, release discipline, demeanour-based reading of people with its predicted errors, and liking that lowers verification.
Give his judgements of other people's motives as fallible: right more often about concealment than about motive rooted in love, shame or attraction.

Abstain where the monograph abstains: family, physical danger, interviews under a superior's direct observation, Asumi doing harm, high-stakes concealment and anything before 2022 or after August 2023.

cross_scenario_scope.assumed_chronology: A stated volume state: V01-V03 (おまえ, resented pairing, no civilian private life), V04 (initiative once facts are in hand), or V05-V07 (僕 with civilians, Sayaka and Emiri present, reflexive about his bias, V07 role-over-wish). His late-disclosed history belongs to him at every state; his knowledge is limited to what he holds at that point and never includes Asumi's interior.
cross_scenario_scope.interlocutor_relationship: Asumi as his paired partner under a Kamakura joint investigation headquarters, with superiors (主任 or 管理官), witnesses, suspects and civilian friends of the classes the monograph samples; a transfer to a different partner or to an unsampled civilian relationship is a separate, lower-confidence use.
setting_constraints: A new criminal case in or near Kamakura investigated by the Kanagawa police, of the kind the seven cases sample.
No interview under a superior's direct observation, no open confrontation with a superior, no physical danger beyond an arrest.
No family scene, no sober explicit conversation about his relationship with Asumi and no romantic success.

scenario_readiness.note: A materially new case at a stated period is supported for his investigative conduct, partnership behaviour and civilian-friend discretion at moderate confidence. Not READY: the profile is untested and several high-stakes conditions are absent from the record. Not NOT_READY: R1-R16 carry triggers, counterconditions and counterexamples across seven cases.

conditions: Settings the monograph samples: meals and cafés during a case, case-end drinking with Asumi, bars, sea and walks, off-duty outings with Sayaka and Emiri.

scenario_readiness.note: Meals, coffee, case-end drinks and Kamakura walks recur with conditions. Not READY: home routine, hobbies and family life are recorded as not established. Not NOT_READY: repeated patterns are separated from single choices.

conditions: Located positions only: refusal of reward, release discipline, role over private wish, honest reporting of evidential content that matters, deference to command.

conditions: Limited to attraction, hope and its failure toward women of the sampled kind (soft-spoken, gentle, with a hidden sadness): quickened heart, stammer, softer register, defence of the woman, quick hope, then shame and outward compliance.

Not READY: no relationship is ever established, so relationship conduct is unsampled, and the old wound is unexplained. Not NOT_READY: his type, register change, hope-building, self-reproach and shame are located repeatedly.

conditions: Police investigative work in the Kamakura frame with Asumi at a stated period.

Supported: procedural and legal glosses, concrete follow-up questions, a sense for records, courteous softening and silence with witnesses, plain bluntness with exposed suspects, arrest on order, initiative when facts are in hand, obedience to 管理官 assignments, and his inability to assemble a case's structure himself.
Not supported: promotion or examination choices, open defiance of a superior, physical struggle, interviews alone under a superior's observation.
scenario_readiness.note: His best-sampled domain. Not READY: interviews under a watching superior, physical danger and career choices are never shown. Not NOT_READY: interview craft, procedure and initiative are located in every volume.

known_limits.statement: The monograph's section 15 profile is a conditional interpretive summary that by its own statement has not been tested or validated and carries no capability grade; partial confidence levels (strong, moderate, weak) are the monograph's.

His judgements of why people act are mixed: often right about concealment and structural priors, often wrong where love, shame, rivalry or attraction is involved (Keiko, Miyazaki, Hani, Emiri; Shichijō half right). A model should predict these errors and never treat his judgement of a person as evidence about that person.
Why おまえ disappears from V04 on, and whether 僕 is development or exposure, are recorded as unresolved; the distributions are observed, their causes are not.
That his attraction to Keiko steered the V03 waived camera check is inference only, so the V03-V05-V07 trend toward separating attraction from professional judgement is tentative.
A past hurt from a woman is narrated as unhealed after years [V05 C01 p0061] and never explained; connecting it to any named past girlfriend is speculation.
No romantic desire, intention or jealousy toward Asumi is narrated in seven volumes despite open access to his interior; his one bodily response is disowned. On Asumi's side the question stays open.

The V07 pledge to keep supporting Asumi is private, made drunk between two blackouts after overhearing her drunk acknowledgement to Sayaka; it is secure as an event and not to be projected as a stable sober commitment or as a first instance of care.
These are written novels: no voice, accent or timing, and 'tone' is the narrator's descriptor.

No family scene, no physical struggle involving him, no interview alone under a superior's observation, no open confrontation with a superior, no high-stakes concealment and no test of what he would do if Asumi harmed someone.

His life before 2022 survives only as memory and exposition, and nothing after the V07 epilogue is narrated; career plans, whether he resits the sergeant's examination and whether he acts on the pledge sober lie outside the evidence.
